First, we use the product rule for radicals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{162} & =\sqrt[3]{27\cdot 6}=\sqrt[3]{27}\cdot \sqrt[3]{6}=3\sqrt[3]{6} & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{7}+5\sqrt[3]{162}-\sqrt[3]{6} & = \\ \sqrt{7}+5(3\sqrt[3]{6})-\sqrt[3]{6}= \\ \sqrt{7}+15\sqrt[3]{6}-\sqrt[3]{6}. & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can combine the two $\sqrt[3]{6}$ terms together:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{7}+15\sqrt[3]{6}-\sqrt[3]{6}= \\ \sqrt{7}+(15\sqrt[3]{6}-\sqrt[3]{6}) & = \\ \sqrt{7}+(15-1)\sqrt[3]{6} & = \\ \sqrt{7}+14\sqrt[3]{6} & \end{aligned}
$$
